item.group_name: Short video from a picture or text
item.title: Five Café Photos With Music

turns.text: Make a 10-second vertical Instagram reel from these five café photos, in the order attached. Add some relaxed instrumental music. No text, just nice smooth transitions.

item.tests: Produces one finished five-photo reel with the requested sequence, smooth transitions and an audible instrumental soundtrack.

answer_sheet.Photos and order: Use all five: storefront, latte, pastries, barista, interior.
answer_sheet.Music and voice: Relaxed instrumental music; no vocals or voiceover. Track choice is your call.
answer_sheet.Transitions and framing: Smooth transitions; other editing and framing choices are your call.

must_haves: One playable vertical reel runs for approximately 10 seconds.
All five supplied café photos appear recognizably in the requested order.
Each photo has enough screen time to be recognizable, rather than appearing only as a flash.
Relaxed instrumental music is audible, with no speech or singing.
Transitions between photos are smooth, and no added text appears.

turns.text: Make a 10-second vertical Instagram reel from these five café photos in the order attached: the storefront pic, the latte pic, the pastries pic, the barista pic, and the interior pic. Add some relaxed instrumental music. No text, just nice smooth transitions. I’m on the free plan and don’t want my credits burned, so please tell me what it will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter, or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
**Nothing has been generated or charged.** The read-only planner quotes **255 credits** for an AI-generated version:

| Item | Credits |
|---|---:|
| Five 2-second clips, in your attached order, vertical 9:16 at 480p | 240 |
| Relaxed instrumental music (15-second minimum, using 10 seconds) | 15 |
| Joining the clips | 0 |
| **Total** | **255** |

These settings support the free plan, but I can’t verify your remaining balance here.

**Important limitation:** the available joining tool makes hard cuts—not smooth crossfades. AI generation may also change details in your photos. I wouldn’t spend 255 credits on that when you mainly want a photo slideshow.

### Cheaper options
- **Recommended: 0 Magic Hour credits.** Assemble the original photos in a free video editor with gentle zooms, crossfades, and a free-to-use instrumental track. This preserves the photos and gives you the smooth transitions you requested.
- **Shorter AI version: about 135 credits** for 5 seconds—one second per photo, plus music. It would feel considerably faster.
- **Without generated music: 240 credits** for the 10-second AI version; add properly licensed music elsewhere.
- **Smaller:** 480p is already the lowest supported resolution for this AI route, so reducing size further isn’t an available saving.

For the free-editor version, use **storefront → latte → pastries → barista → interior**, roughly two seconds each, with short crossfades, adjusting overlaps to keep the total at 10 seconds.

Would you like step-by-step free-editor instructions, or do you want to approve an AI option despite the hard-cut limitation?
dialog.user: ok, go ahead with that—the free-editor instructions for the 0-credit version.

turns.agent:
Here’s the **0–Magic Hour-credit route** using a free editor such as **CapCut or VN**. Use only free effects and your own or properly licensed music—no AI generation needed.

### 1. Set up the reel
- Create a new project in **vertical 9:16**.
- Import the photos in this order:
  1. Storefront
  2. Latte
  3. Pastries
  4. Barista
  5. Interior
- Remove any automatic ending clip or template text.

### 2. Fit the photos
For the wide photos, use a **blurred copy of the photo as the background**, keeping the full original visible in front. This avoids cutting off the storefront, barista, or interior. Alternatively, crop to fill and reposition each photo carefully.

### 3. Set timing and transitions
- Start with **2 seconds per photo**.
- Add a **0.3-second Dissolve/Crossfade** between each pair.
- Check the total timeline length. Some editors overlap clips during transitions, shortening the reel.
  - If four transitions reduce the runtime to **8.8 seconds**, extend each photo to **2.24 seconds** to restore **10 seconds**.
  - Otherwise, keep two seconds each.

### 4. Add gentle movement
Apply a subtle **slow zoom-in** to each photo—approximately **100% to 105%** using start/end keyframes. Keep the movement small so it feels relaxed rather than busy.

### 5. Add music
- Choose a mellow **instrumental acoustic guitar, piano, or lo-fi** track.
- Use music you own or that’s licensed for your intended Instagram use. For a café/business account, don’t assume every in-app track permits commercial use.
- Trim it to **10 seconds**.
- Add a short fade-in and a **0.5–1-second fade-out**.
- Leave captions, stickers, and text off.

### 6. Export
Choose **1080 × 1920, 30 fps, MP4**. Exporting larger won’t add detail to these photos, but it gives you a standard Reel format. For a smaller file, **720 × 1280** is fine.

**Final check:** 10 seconds • correct photo order • four smooth dissolves • instrumental music • no text or automatic end card.

Here’s the **0–Magic Hour-credit route** using a free editor such as **CapCut or VN**. Use only free effects and your own or properly licensed music—no AI generation needed.

### 1. Set up the reel
- Create a new project in **vertical 9:16**.
- Import the photos in this order:
  1. Storefront
  2. Latte
  3. Pastries
  4. Barista
  5. Interior
- Remove any automatic ending clip or template text.

### 2. Fit the photos
For the wide photos, use a **blurred copy of the photo as the background**, keeping the full original visible in front. This avoids cutting off the storefront, barista, or interior. Alternatively, crop to fill and reposition each photo carefully.

### 3. Set timing and transitions
- Start with **2 seconds per photo**.
- Add a **0.3-second Dissolve/Crossfade** between each pair.
- Check the total timeline length. Some editors overlap clips during transitions, shortening the reel.
  - If four transitions reduce the runtime to **8.8 seconds**, extend each photo to **2.24 seconds** to restore **10 seconds**.
  - Otherwise, keep two seconds each.

### 4. Add gentle movement
Apply a subtle **slow zoom-in** to each photo—approximately **100% to 105%** using start/end keyframes. Keep the movement small so it feels relaxed rather than busy.

### 5. Add music
- Choose a mellow **instrumental acoustic guitar, piano, or lo-fi** track.
- Use music you own or that’s licensed for your intended Instagram use. For a café/business account, don’t assume every in-app track permits commercial use.
- Trim it to **10 seconds**.
- Add a short fade-in and a **0.5–1-second fade-out**.
- Leave captions, stickers, and text off.

### 6. Export
Choose **1080 × 1920, 30 fps, MP4**. Exporting larger won’t add detail to these photos, but it gives you a standard Reel format. For a smaller file, **720 × 1280** is fine.

**Final check:** 10 seconds • correct photo order • four smooth dissolves • instrumental music • no text or automatic end card.
